data.title: Kitchen Dissolving Lab
data.description: Explore what happens when you mix different kitchen items in water and discover how to get them back.

substances.name: Table Salt
substances.imagePrompt: A small bowl of white table salt crystals

substances.name: Sugar
substances.imagePrompt: A scoop of granulated white sugar

substances.name: Sand
substances.imagePrompt: A small pile of golden beach sand

substances.name: Cooking Oil
substances.imagePrompt: Golden cooking oil in a glass

separationMethods.description: Heat the mixture so the liquid turns into gas and escapes into the air, leaving the solid behind.
separationMethods.animation: liquid boils away leaving solid crystals

separationMethods.description: Pour the mixture through a paper filter that traps solid pieces while letting liquid pass through.
separationMethods.animation: liquid passes through paper trap while solid stays behind

separationMethods.description: Carefully pour the top liquid layer off the bottom liquid layer when they do not mix together.
separationMethods.animation: top liquid layer pours off gently

challenges.instruction: How would you recover Table Salt from a mixture where it has been stirred into water?
challenges.hint: Think about what happens to the liquid when heat is applied over time.
challenges.narration: Heat makes the liquid turn into vapor, leaving the solid behind just like salt crystals forming on a beach!

challenges.instruction: How would you separate a mixture of Sand and water?
challenges.hint: Use a barrier with tiny holes that catches solid bits while letting liquid flow through.
challenges.narration: Great job! The barrier traps the solid pieces while letting the liquid pass right through.

challenges.instruction: How would you separate a mixture of Cooking Oil and water?
challenges.hint: Since these two liquids form separate layers, you can carefully pour the top one off.
challenges.narration: You got it! Because the liquids form distinct layers, pouring off the top layer separates them neatly.
